_comment_file: The audit log viewer: the table, its filter bar, its event vocabulary, and the export dialog. This screen is what someone reads after an incident, so precision beats warmth everywhere in this file. Two rules that apply to the whole namespace: (1) nothing here may overstate what the log guarantees — see header.guarantee; (2) the words in `outcome` and `category` appear both on a filter chip and in a table cell, and a reader matching one against the other needs them to be the same word, so translate each of them once and reuse that choice.

header._comment_: The bar across the top of the screen. `back` returns to the main window; this screen owns the whole window while it is open.
header.title: 审计日志
header._comment_badge: A status badge, not a sentence: the log is append-only and it never leaves this machine. Lower case and very short — it sits in a 20px pill. The middle dot is a separator and may be replaced with whatever separates two short labels in your language.
header._comment_refresh: A verb on a button: re-read the log from the vault.
header._comment_export: A verb on a button. The ellipsis is the convention for 'this opens a dialog and does not act immediately'; keep it, in whatever form your language writes it.
header._comment_guarantee: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Do not soften, shorten or summarise this, and do not translate it as 'tamper-proof' or 'tamper-evident' — the log is neither, and saying so is the entire point of the sentence. Both halves must survive: nobody outside the vault can read or change the log, AND anyone who can open the vault can edit it undetected. If the second half will not fit, make the first half shorter. See docs/features/recording-audit.md.
header.guarantee: 打不开这个保险库的人，既读不到也改不了这份日志——但能打开它的人可以随意修改这份日志，而 Remoter 察觉不到。
header._comment_recordings: Says why there is no recording player on a screen where someone would look for one. 'v0.2' is a version number and is not translated.
header.recordings: 目前还没有录像播放器：会话录制要到 v0.2 才有，所以也没有任何录像可以播放。

columns._comment_: Table column headers. Single words where possible; the columns are narrow.
columns._comment_who: The column naming the operating-system account and the computer that wrote each entry. One short word; the column is narrow.
columns._comment_whoTitle: SECURITY-ADJACENT. The tooltip on the Who column header. The names are what each computer's operating system reported, and anybody who can open the vault can write any entry; keep 'not proof of identity' unsoftened.
columns.whoTitle: 写入这条记录的账户和计算机，以该计算机操作系统报告的为准。它能区分可以打开这个保险库的人，但不能证明身份。
columns._comment_node: A node is a connection or folder in the tree. See the glossary.
columns._comment_detail: The column holding the core's own short note about an entry. That note arrives already written and is not translated here.

table._comment_label: The accessible name of the table itself. Read aloud before the rows.
table.label: 审计记录
table._comment_loadFailed: A heading over the core's own error message, which appears beneath it.
table.filtersFailed: 无法读取日志的筛选项列表。
table.nodesFailed: 无法读取连接树，因此节点筛选不可用。
table._comment_actorsFailed: A heading over the core's own error message, when the list of accounts for the Who filter could not be read.
table.actorsFailed: 无法读取账户列表，因此“操作者”筛选不可用。
table._comment_actorUnrecorded: In the Who column for an entry written before Remoter recorded who wrote entries, or by a copy of Remoter that could not tell. It means 'this was not recorded', never 'nobody'.
table._comment_actorTitle: The tooltip on a Who cell. {account} is an account name (possibly DOMAIN\user), {machine} a computer name — both user data, isolated before they arrive. {os} is an operating system's proper name such as Windows or macOS, never translated.
table._comment_rowLoading: Shown in a row whose page has not arrived yet. One word: it sits in the Time column of a 28px row.
table._comment_noValue: An em dash standing for 'this entry has no value in this column'. Replace it only if your language uses a different glyph for an empty table cell; it is not a word.
table._comment_removedNode: The entry names a node that has since been deleted from the tree. Parenthesised because it is an aside about a missing value, not a value.
table._comment_eventTitle: The tooltip on an event cell. {event} is the event name exactly as stored in the log — a machine identifier such as `host_key_changed`, never translated, because it is what someone greps an export for. {category} is one of the words under `category` below.
table._comment_appendOnly: SECURITY-ADJACENT. In the footer, next to a shield. The second sentence is the one that matters: exporting is a copy, not a move, and nothing an export does removes an entry. Do not drop it.
table.appendOnly: 记录只会追加，绝不会被改写。导出只是复制它们，不会把它们移走。
table._comment_shown: The row counter in the footer. {first} and {last} are the numbers of the first and last rows currently drawn, {total} how many match the filter — all three already formatted for this locale, so they arrive as text. The en dash joins the two ends of a range; the middle dot separates the count from the note after it. 'rendered as you scroll' explains why the table holds only a few rows at a time.
table.shown: 第 {first}–{last} 行，共 {total} 行 · 随滚动逐步渲染
table._comment_shownNone: Replaces `shown` when the filter matches nothing.

empty._comment_: The whole-table empty state. It is a filter result, never an empty log: a vault that has been opened has at least one entry in it.
empty.title: 没有符合这些筛选条件的记录。
empty.hint: 把时间范围放宽，或者清除筛选条件。
empty._comment_clear: A verb on a button: put every filter back to its default.

outcome._comment_: How an audited action ended, in the Outcome column and on the outcome filter chips. Each is a past-tense statement about the action, not a label for a state: the action succeeded, failed, or was refused. Keep them distinct — `failed` and `denied` are different findings in an incident review, and a translation that merges them loses that. Each word is also carried by a glyph and a colour, so it can be short.
outcome._comment_denied: Refused by a policy check: the action was understood and not permitted. Not a malfunction.
outcome._comment_unknown: An outcome written by a newer build of Remoter that this one has no word for. Shown rather than dropping the row.

category._comment_: The filter chips, and the second half of a row's tooltip. `node` and `connection` are the pair to be careful with: `node` means a change to an entry in the tree — created, renamed, deleted — and `connection` means an attempt to actually reach a host. They are different questions, and neither may be translated as a bare 'Connections'.
category._comment_warning: The chip an incident review presses first: everything that did not succeed, plus a few events that are worth reading whatever their outcome.
category._comment_other: The category of an event this build does not recognise.

event._comment_: What happened, in the Event column. Each key is the event's stored spelling and mirrors AuditEvent in crates/remoter-vault/src/storage.rs; an event written by a newer build has no key here and is shown as its stored spelling instead. Every one of these is a past-tense statement of a completed action — the Outcome column beside it says whether it worked, so 'Vault unlocked' with an outcome of 'Failed' means an unlock was attempted and refused. Do not add 'successfully' to any of them.
event._comment_vault_unlock_failed: A distinct event from vault_unlocked with a failed outcome: this one is recorded when the attempt never got as far as a key.
event._comment_vault_migrated: The vault file was upgraded to a newer on-disk schema.
event._comment_slot_added: A key slot is one way of opening the vault — a password, a key file, a security key, a recovery key. Adding one gives someone a new way in, which is why it is audited.
event._comment_password_changed: The vault password, not a password stored in the vault.
event._comment_master_key_rotated: The key everything else is encrypted under was replaced. The largest single operation the vault performs.
event._comment_kdf_upgraded: The key derivation function's cost was raised to the current floor, so an existing password now takes longer to try. KDF is a technical abbreviation; use whatever your language's security writing uses, or leave it.
event._comment_node_created: 'Entry' here means one item in the connection tree — a connection, a folder or a credential.
event._comment_node_moved: Reparented or reordered within the tree.
event._comment_secret_used: The secret was decrypted and handed to a protocol to open a connection. It was never shown to anyone.
event._comment_secret_revealed: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The secret was displayed on screen. This is the entry an incident review looks for, and it must not read like `secret_used` — the difference between a secret being used and a secret being shown to a person is the whole reason both are logged.
event.secret_revealed: 机密已在屏幕上显示给人看
event._comment_secret_exported: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The secret was written to a file outside the vault, in the clear.
event.secret_exported: 机密已明文写入导出文件
event._comment_trust_pinned: A host key or certificate was accepted and remembered, so this host will be recognised next time.
event._comment_trust_rejected: SECURITY-CRITICAL. A host key or certificate was refused — which, when the host was previously trusted, is what a machine-in-the-middle attempt looks like from here. Do not soften it into 'not accepted'.
event._comment_setting_changed: An application or vault setting was changed. The Detail column names which.

filters._comment_: The filter bar above the table. Its vocabulary comes from the core, so a chip can appear for a category this file has no word for.
filters._comment_region: The accessible name of the bar as a whole.
filters._comment_timeLabel: The label on the time-range control. One word — it sits beside the control, not above it.

range._comment_: The time windows on offer. Each is measured backwards from the moment the filter was last changed, not from midnight.
range._comment_all: No lower bound at all — the whole history the vault holds.

filters._comment_categories: The accessible name of the group of category chips.
filters._comment_outcomes: The accessible name of the group of outcome chips.
filters._comment_loadingVocabulary: Read out while the chips are still skeletons. The chips are not guessed: the list of categories and outcomes is the log's own, so it has to be fetched before any chip can be drawn.
filters.loadingVocabulary: 正在读取日志自带的筛选项列表…
filters._comment_anyNode: The first option in the node filter: do not narrow by node. It also matches the entries that concern no node at all.
filters._comment_nodesLoading: The tooltip on the node filter while the tree is still being read, which is why the control is disabled.
filters._comment_nodeOption: One option in the node filter. {name} is the entry's name and {host} its hostname or address — both user data, in any script, and both isolated before they arrive so neither can reorder the other. The em dash separates them; it is not a word.
filters._comment_whoLabel: The label on the Who filter: narrow the log to entries written by one account on one computer. One word, beside the control.
filters._comment_anyone: The first option in the Who filter: do not narrow by who wrote an entry. It also matches entries whose writer was not recorded.
filters._comment_actorsLoading: The tooltip on the Who filter while the list of accounts is still being read, which is why the control is disabled.
filters.actorsLoading: 正在读取谁写入过这份日志…
filters._comment_whoOption: One option in the Who filter. {account} is an account name and {machine} a computer name — both user data, isolated before they arrive. The em dash separates them; it is not a word.
filters._comment_matching: How many entries the current filter matches, shown at the end of the bar. Terse on purpose: it sits beside the filters it describes, so it does not repeat the word 'entries'.

export._comment_: The export dialog. Two things it says out loud, because both change whether someone should press the button: the export is itself written into the log, and the file it writes is not encrypted.
export.title: 导出审计日志
export._comment_audited: SECURITY-ADJACENT. Exporting appends a row to the log saying an export happened. Someone who expects a silent read and finds the row afterwards has been surprised by their own tool, so this is said before the fact and must not be dropped.
export.audited: 导出会往这份日志里追加一条记录。导出本身就是一项被审计的操作。
export._comment_plaintext: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The heading of a warning callout. 'Not encrypted' is the load-bearing phrase; do not translate it as 'less protected' or 'unprotected by default'.
export.plaintext: 文件写在保险库之外，并且不加密。
export._comment_plaintextBody: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The body of that callout. Both halves are needed: the file holds no passwords or key material, AND it holds a full history of which hosts were reached and when. Reassurance without the second half is misleading.
export.plaintextBody: 它记录的是发生了什么、在什么时候、针对哪台主机——里面没有密码，也没有密钥材料，但有您连接活动的完整历史。任何能读到这个文件的人，都能读到这段历史。
export.formatHelp: JSON 保留字段原本存储的样子。CSV 可以用电子表格打开。
export._comment_json: A file format name. Not translated, in any language or script.
export._comment_csv: A file format name. Not translated, in any language or script.
export._comment_scopeLabel: Which entries to write. The label above a pair of radio buttons.
export._comment_scopeFiltered: Everything the filter on the screen behind matches — which is more than the rows currently drawn.
export.scopeFiltered: 您当前正在查看的那些记录
export._comment_scopeHelp: Says exactly what 'the entries you are looking at' covers, because the obvious reading — the dozen rows on screen — is the wrong one.
export.scopeHelp: 筛选条件作用于您选定的整个时间范围，而不是屏幕上的这一页。
export._comment_pathLabel: Where to write the file. Also the accessible name of the text field.
export._comment_pathPlaceholder: An example of a file path, shown in an empty field. Adapt it to the path convention a reader of your language would recognise, but keep it an example and keep it a path.
export._comment_browse: The button that opens the system file dialog. The ellipsis marks it as leading to another window.
export._comment_browseFailed: Shown under the field when the system dialog refuses to open. The second sentence is the way out and must survive.
export.browseFailed: 系统文件对话框没有打开。请改为直接输入路径。
export._comment_pathMissing: A validation message, shown under the field and as the export button's tooltip. Imperative: it says what to do, not what went wrong.
export.pathMissing: 请先选择文件写到哪里。
export._comment_submit: The button that performs the export. A verb.
export._comment_busy: Read out while the file is being written, in place of the button's label.
export._comment_done: The heading of the callout that replaces the form once the file is written.
export._comment_doneDetail: {count} is how many entries were written, {path} the file that was written (isolated, so a path in another script cannot reorder the sentence), {size} its size already formatted for this locale. The last sentence is deliberate: it tells the reader that the log they were just looking at has changed, so a row they did not expect is not a sign of something wrong.
export.doneDetail: {count, plural, other {已把 # 条记录}}写入 {path}（{size}）。记录这次导出的那一行，现在就在日志的最上面。
